what: Eaton makes the equipment that moves and controls electrical power: switchgear, circuit breakers, transformers, uninterruptible power supplies and the components that go inside data centres, factories, buildings, aircraft and vehicles.
customers: Data centre operators, utilities, construction contractors, industrial manufacturers, aerospace firms and vehicle makers, mostly in North America and Europe.
money: power distribution and control equipment for North and South America
the same equipment outside the Americas
hydraulics, fuel and power systems for aircraft
drivetrain components and electric-vehicle power systems
moat: Equipment that has to be certified and specified into a building or aircraft design, long lead times that lock in orders, and a service network close to customers.
risks: Data centre orders are concentrated among a few large buyers whose spending can pause
Construction and industrial demand follow the economic cycle
Debt of about $20 billion was raised partly for acquisitions
Competitors are expanding capacity for the same electrical demand
opportunities: Electricity demand from data centres, grid upgrades and electrification is growing faster than the wider economy
A long order backlog gives visibility on revenue for several quarters
Aerospace aftermarket work carries higher margins than new equipment
watch: The orders-to-sales ratio and the backlog, which show whether demand is still running ahead of deliveries.
